anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Physical data-model structures, indexing, partitioning, or column definitions do not align with workload access paths, forcing inefficient scans and extra look-ups.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level runtime settings for memory, logging, parallelism, and background workers are mis-tuned relative to hardware and workload, introducing artificial bottlenecks or bursts of maintenance activity.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Downstream replicas cannot receive, persist, or apply primary transaction-log traffic at source speed, causing growing apply lag and retention of log segments.

When all three root causes are present simultaneously, the system exhibits a blended symptom set: primary queries show high latency and erratic plan shapes (full scans, excessive random I/O); checkpoint, log-write, and work-memory waits spike even though raw CPU and I/O remain under-utilised; at the same time replica lag widens rapidly, retention of log segments inflates primary disk usage, and read-only workloads on replicas see increasingly stale data. Performance troubleshooting becomes harder because any point-in-time metric may show multiple saturated subsystems (buffer cache churn, background writer thrashing, replication apply backlog), yet none individually explains the full degradation.

Causal interaction: poorly designed schemas generate larger row sets and bloated indexes, inflating the volume of dirty pages and redo that the primary must handle. Mis-configured memory and checkpoint parameters then accelerate flush storms, fragment the buffer cache, or throttle worker memory, amplifying query cost and redo generation even further. The swollen and bursty log stream must be shipped to replicas, but their apply threads—already contending with the same inefficient schema structure—fall behind, creating replication lag. As log segments cannot be recycled until all replicas acknowledge them, disk pressure on the primary rises, triggering additional checkpoints and background cleanup that again interact with the mis-tuned parameters. The three root causes therefore reinforce each other in a feedback loop that degrades primary throughput, replica freshness, and overall system stability far more severely than any single anomaly alone.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
